solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A bad-tempered over

parts.note: someone bad-tempered is cross

explanation.surface: A cricket over bowled by a grumpy bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; here 'over' is the definition, as a preposition meaning from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: going over a road and going to the other side of it are the same movement.

clue.text: I'm upset over Society leader's bad behaviour

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting over the next comes before it
upset means knocked over, so the two letters are turned round, which reads upwards in a down clue

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a leader or head is a chief

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by the poor conduct of a society's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the two letters round, which in a down answer means reading them upwards; 'leader' looks like it picks a first letter but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: naughty conduct, especially by children, is mischief.

clue.text: Holder seen playing in short trousers

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters romping about into a new order

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper seen playing in shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the letters of HOLDER SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are Bavarian leather shorts, a kind of short trousers.

clue.text: Everyone I set up and make fun of becomes uncomfortable

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: everyone means all
to make fun of someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A person who is mocked by everyone they have set up ends up uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ALL I into ILLA, which is then followed by TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: feeling awkward or uneasy is a phrase meaning uncomfortable.

clue.text: After short time humour a fool

indicators.note: after says the humour piece follows the time piece

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
wit is humour

explanation.surface: After a brief while, someone humours a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' looks like a verb, humouring the fool, but it is the noun WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a twit is a silly person, a fool.

clue.text: Charge round old room

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to lunge is to charge forward

explanation.surface: A fee charged for an old room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee; it is a sudden forward thrust, LUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lounge is a sitting room in a house or hotel.

clue.text: Make known girl's put on a little weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's name is placed on top of the weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Gossip reveals that a girl has gained a little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on a little weight' reads as gaining weight; 'put on' instead stacks the name above the weight in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to announce something is to make it known publicly.

clue.text: Ring artist exhibiting a monster

parts.note: a bell's ring is a chime
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painting of a monster shown at the ring of a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a common way crosswords give 'artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera is a fire-breathing beast of Greek myth, made of lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Singer in musical, touring

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A singer appears in a touring musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across musicAL TOuring.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an alto is a singer with a lower female or high male voice.

clue.text: Information from base

explanation.surface: Getting the details from headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it means inside facts; as low-down it is an adjective for something contemptibly mean.

clue.text: Horse and cart ordered for a band

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A horse and cart is ordered to carry a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges HORSE CART; 'and' just joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an orchestra is a band of musicians.

clue.text: Dance with beat and vitality

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: A dance done with rhythm and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' sounds musical in a dance clue; here it means thrash, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Son's desire to become smart

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a desire is a wish

explanation.surface: A son wants to look stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something swish is smart or fashionable.

clue.text: Oriental festival's name

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: An Eastern festival and what it is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: oriental and eastern both describe things from the East.

clue.text: It can still be served on a round plate!

definitions.text: It can still be served on a round plate!

parts.words: It can still be served on a round plate!
parts.note: the joke is that a '... needn't come on a square plate: the phrase means a filling meal

explanation.surface: A joke about the shape of dinnerware.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hearty, nourishing meal is called a square one, whatever the crockery.

clue.text: Little Arthur's masterpiece?

parts.note: Art is a short form of Arthur, so something he produced is a piece of work by Art

explanation.surface: A child named Arthur proudly shows off his best creation.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is a fine piece of art; the phrase also reads as a creation by someone called Art.

clue.text: Broken foot? She's to rearrange tap dance

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: to shuffle cards is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken foot has to rearrange plans for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges FOOT SHE'S into SOFTSHOE; then 'to rearrange' is not a second signal but the synonym SHUFFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the soft-shoe shuffle is a tap-style dance done in soft-soled shoes.

clue.text: Boat user at sea, a wrecker

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone using a boat at sea causes a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges BOAT USER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a saboteur deliberately wrecks or damages things.

clue.text: Female, one having to live in the home

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to live somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: A woman who has to live in the family home.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonym: the fireside stands for home and family life, as in fireside chats.

clue.text: Bohemian to attend, with family backing

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the family word is read in reverse

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: An unconventional type attends with family support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to attend' gives BE AT; 'backing' turns KIN into NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a beatnik was a 1950s bohemian of the Beat Generation.

clue.text: Animal in mountain pasture, a cat with no tail

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain pasture

indicators.note: with no tail says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An animal grazes in mountain pasture with a tailless cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' takes the last letter T from CAT, leaving CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the alpaca is a South American animal related to the llama.

clue.text: Starts to ring up rap artist living in the countryside

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone phones a rap artist who lives in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of ring up rap artist living give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rural describes what belongs to or is in the countryside.

clue.text: Acquire gold carriage

parts.note: to land a prize is to acquire it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a gold-plated carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Car from former company

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A car bought from a firm that no longer trades.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across forMER Company.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal abbreviation: a Merc is a Mercedes car.

clue.text: Subject suggested by principal in charge

parts.note: principal means chief or top

explanation.surface: A subject proposed by the head teacher in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like the head of a school; it is the adjective meaning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a topic is a subject for discussion.

clue.text: Person in charge getting rid of one cook

indicators.note: getting rid of says a letter is removed from the person in charge

parts.note: a chief is a person in charge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boss sacks one of the cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting rid of one' sounds like a dismissal; it takes I out of CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a chef is a professional cook.

clue.text: Frank moans about lodger?

parts.note: frank and free both mean open and unrestrained in speech

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank complains about a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodger' suggests a tenant; here it is a member of a Masonic lodge, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: Freemasons meet in lodges, so a member is whimsically a lodger.

clue.text: Pawnbroker with a ring, initially doubtful

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker with a ring is at first unsure of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' as a nickname for a pawnbroker is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something unclear is uncertain or doubtful.

clue.text: Female spies receiving praise

indicators.note: receiving means the spies take the praise inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A woman spy gets commended by her agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' is a cryptic way to define a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Claudia is a female first name.
